verdict.rationale: The pipeline retrieved verbatim body text from many irs.gov guidance pages: the EIN page, the SS-4 filing addresses, the MeF overview, the e-file provider enrollment page, IRIS, the Pub 525 update and mobile-friendly forms. That shows the public reading surface served real HTML content to a keyless agent, not a JS-only shell or CAPTCHA. The only denials observed were the 403 on the /dmaf signed-form entry and the 503 on the app-host robots.txt; both are transactional or app hosts, not guidance pages, and the 404s on llms.txt and .md were normal server responses rather than bot walls. Missing for 10: an explicit HTTP-200 probe record of a guidance page under the identified UA, independent corroboration across repeated or bulk fetches, and confirmation that no rate-based bot challenge appears at scale.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface
